{
  "jobspec": "#!/bin/bash

# Flux batch script
#
# This is a self-submitting Flux script: run it directly (e.g., `./combine_d1_output.flux.sh`).
# It will submit itself to Flux with the translated resource requests.

# Translated resources from Slurm:
#   --nodes=1            -> -N 1
#   --ntasks-per-node=1  -> -n 1
#   --cpus-per-task=1    -> -c 1
#   --time=5:00:00       -> -t 5h
JOBID=$(flux batch -N 1 -n 1 -c 1 -t 5h --wrap "bash $0 __flux_inner")

echo "Submitted Flux job: $JOBID"

if [ "${1:-}" = "__flux_inner" ]; then
  # NOTE: Slurm --job-name=combine-d1-output not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: job identification may be less convenient; runtime performance is unaffected.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mem-per-cpu=250m not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a per-core memory reservation/limit, the job may contend for memory or be OOM-killed, affecting reliability/performance.

  # NOTE: Slurm --account=pschloss1 not translated.
  # Performance/ops implication: accounting/charging may not be applied as intended; site may require account/project out-of-band.

  # NOTE: Slurm --partition=standard not translated.
  # Performance implication: without a queue/constraint mapping, the job may run on any eligible resources; you are not forcing the standard partition.

  # NOTE: Slurm --mail-user/--mail-type not translated.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: no email notifications.

  # NOTE: Slurm --output=%x-%j.out uses %x/%j expansions which Flux does not provide portably.
  # Performance implication: none; operational implication: log filename may not be unique unless you add uniqueness.

  # NOTE: Slurm --export=ALL not translated.
  # Performance implication: usually none (Flux typically inherits the environment), but if your site sanitizes environments, missing exports could change runtime behavior.

  mkdir -p logs/slurm/

  flux run -n 1 -c 1 bash code/bash/family_d1_cat_csv_files.sh
fi
"
}
